sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Immunofluorescence microscopy confirmed expression of tagged full-length protein in stably transduced HEK-293T cells (L4); fluorescent protein fusions (Clover, ~240 aa; Ruby2, ~240 aa) were also tolerated at this junction (L2), demonstrating that large C-terminal inserts do not prevent folding or membrane insertion. Adiponectin-receptor function was NOT MEASURED in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: ADIPOR2 has an inverted topology: the N-terminus (1–145) is intracellular and the C-terminus (370–386) is extracellular. A C-terminal HA tag therefore lands on the extracellular face. Python confirmed residue 386 = L, 17 residues from the last TM helix (349–369), well above the ≥3-residue minimum. L2 further shows that even a ~240 aa fluorescent protein is tolerated at this exact junction, making a short ALFA-tag insert highly plausible. L1 is the primary citation; L2, L3, and L4 corroborate the same position. Full-length ADIPOR2-HA construct cloned into a lentiviral expression vector (pHRSIN-PSFFV) and stably expressed in HEK-293T cells; the HA tag is encoded by primers at the C-terminus of the coding sequence. The same C-terminal junction also carries an S-epitope tag (ADIPOR2-S, L3) and fluorescent protein fusions (ADIPOR2-HA-Clover, ADIPOR2-HA-Ruby2, L2), all confirmed by immunofluorescence microscopy (L4). The C-terminus (residues 370–386) is extracellular per the authoritative topology landmarks, 17 residues from the last TM boundary (349–369).

sources.claim: The coding sequences of ADIPOR2 and SCD1 were amplified from cDNA isolated from HEK‐293T cells using primers encoding a C‐terminal HA tag and cloned into pHRSIN‐P SFFV ‐GFP‐P PGK ‐Hygromycin R (Demaison et al , 2002 ), replacing GFP with the transgene.

literature_notes: L2 (ADIPOR2-HA-Clover / ADIPOR2-HA-Ruby2) and L3 (ADIPOR2-S) and L4 (immunofluorescence confirmation) all converge on the same C-terminal junction as L1 and do not define an independent site; they are cited as corroborating evidence for the single site. L5 describes an N-terminal HA tag (HA::AdipoR2); the N-terminus of ADIPOR2 is intracellular (residues 1–145 per topology landmarks), so this tag is cytoplasmic and is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports an insertion in any of the four short extracellular loops (169–181, 235–245, 295–310).

literature_other_positions.note: HA::AdipoR2 carries an N-terminal HA tag, but the ADIPOR2 N-terminus (residues 1–145) is intracellular per the authoritative topology landmarks; this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular space.
